how: Sanctioned WCA speedcubing competitions have been held in Chicago (West Side Cube Clash 2023 at Intentional Sports), with a regional Wisconsin and Illinois speedcubing community.
IVGDA Chicago and DePaul University host Chicago sites of the annual 48-hour Global Game Jam, the latter described as the city's longest-running game jam.
venue: IGDA Chicago / DePaul University Global Game Jam

how: Northwestern Sailing Center in Evanston offers windsurfing lessons and rentals on Lake Michigan to the public.
Chicago Freediving, an SSI dive center, lists freediving programs plus snorkel and mermaid courses on the North Side.
Chicago SUP Yoga holds seasonal stand-up paddleboard yoga classes on Lake Michigan, run from Montrose Beach and North Avenue Beach.
Sandip Burman teaches sitar in person in Chicagoland (and online) through the World Music Foundation, with sitars available to borrow at the Chicago location.
Chicago Sake School runs tasting classes ('Sake Immersion') covering sake production at Murasake Sake Lounge; no hands-on brewing found.
Chicago Meat Collective and city butcher-shop restaurants have run whole-hog butchery and sausage-making workshops, with The Chopping Block listing butchery classes.
venue: Chicago Meat Collective / The Chopping Block

how: The Chicago Coin Club, founded in 1919, holds monthly meetings downtown with speakers and show-and-tell for collectors.
An informal Chicagoland urbex community photographs abandoned sites, mostly unsanctioned (trespass); no licensed tours found.

how: Sumi-e style ink painting is taught in occasional workshops, such as a Chinatown fan-painting session with artist Liping Zhang and bamboo ink painting at Ingrid's Originals.
venue: Ingrid's Originals / Chinatown Visitor Center workshops

how: Zhaoqiu He's Chinese American art center presents Cantonese opera by senior performers at the Chicago Public Library Chinatown branch, and UChicago has a Chinese Opera Society; no Teochew opera found.
venue: Chinatown Branch, Chicago Public Library (Cantonese opera)

how: Occasional batik workshops run in the metro area, such as a 14+ three-session batik course in Evanston and one-off events at Hyde Park Art Center.
The Fire Arts Center of Chicago teaches beginning and intermediate stone carving in alabaster, sandstone and limestone, and sculptors run one-day stone workshops.
RedBar Crew Chicago and the Watch Collectors' Club hold in-person watch meetups, and retailers such as Burdeen's Jewelry host collector events.
Listen & Learn offers one-on-one Tamil lessons with native tutors in Chicago, in person or online, and Chicago Tamil Sangam advertises classes for children and adults.
The Roosevelt Road overpass beside Union Station is a well-known railfan viewing spot, with guides to other safe spots along Metra and freight corridors.
Vintage toy collectors shop at Toy de Jour in Chicago and at periodic toy shows (Chicago Toy Soldier Show, G.I. Joe and vintage toy buying shows), though most shows are held in suburban hotels.
Kites are flown on the Lake Michigan shoreline at Montrose Harbor and Cricket Hill, home of the city's Kids and Kites Fest; Chicago Kite also stages demonstrations.
Chicago Freediving, an SSI center, offers snorkel tours and snorkel diver programs, and Snorkel Great Lakes runs guided Lake Michigan wreck snorkeling.
Chicago Gamelan (Friends of the Gamelan and Chicago Balinese Gamelan) rehearse Javanese and Balinese ensembles several nights a week in Bridgeport, and all are welcome to participate.
The UIC Linux User Group CTF team meets bi-weekly on campus with beginner-friendly picoCTF sessions, though it is aimed at UIC students; vendor-hosted CTF events also occur.
RefugeeOne's In-Home Adult Mentorship program matches adult volunteers one-to-one with recently arrived refugees on Chicago's far north side, with training provided.
Windy City Harvest runs urban agriculture education and vertical farming and aquaponics programs, and Urban Eden Farms has listed a Hydroponics 101 workshop for adults.
Go Ape's Treetop Adventure at Bemis Woods in Western Springs offers ziplines, aerial obstacles and treetop nets in the forest canopy, roughly 30 km west of the Loop.
